$description: Ergo Light — tool-agnostic design tokens. Layer 1 (primitive ramps) + Layer 2 (semantic roles). Adapters in theme/generate.clj translate semantic tokens into per-tool files; no tool reads this file directly. Ramps built in OKLCH: an eased perceptual L* ladder (steps compress toward the light end so background tints get more resolution), a single locked hue per ramp, and one shared chroma ceiling (~0.045 across the ink steps 300-700) so every accent carries equal weight. Light-end steps 100/200 sit on a three-tier tint scale — whisper ~1.13:1, standard ~1.30:1, strong ~1.55:1 vs paper (a lightness ladder, unchanged by the chroma level) — so state washes read across displays, not just calibrated ones; those wash steps are near-neutral (C≈0.011-0.017, uniform across hues) so they read as barely-tinted paper rather than colour blocks (see primitive.$description for the two-regime chroma model). Cool-monochrome direction: calm neutral paper (one shared bg), soft ink ~8:1, near-grey 'dusty' accents (uniform low chroma, ~4.9:1 at the .600 step), very soft near-neutral background tints. Roles that once separated on hue now lean on the preserved L* ladders.

primitive.$description: Layer 1 — raw color ramps, hue + lightness (50 lightest, 900 darkest). Eased in perceptual L* (steps compress toward the light end) with a single locked hue. TWO CHROMA REGIMES by design: light steps (50-200) are near-neutral background tints (C≈0.006-0.017, low enough that state washes read as barely-tinted paper, not colour blocks), then chroma steps up to a muted 'ink' plateau (C≈0.045) across 300-700. Within that plateau the roles split by lightness, not chroma: the light end (300, L≈0.82) is the strong background 'pop' tier — selection, active search, diff word-emph — while the AA-readable foregrounds live at the dark end (600-700, ~4.8-6.1:1 on paper). The L* ladder is SHARED across every ramp: step N has the same lightness — hence the same contrast — in gray as in any hue, so contrast is a property of the step, not the ramp. 300 is NOT a foreground step (~1.5:1); it only shares the plateau's chroma so a strong-tier background carries the same hue weight as an accent. The 200→300 chroma jump (~+0.028) is intentional: backgrounds stay quiet, foregrounds carry the hue, and the seam lands exactly on the wash→pop boundary. (Amber's light end runs a touch warmer in hue than the other tints — see the amber ramp.) Meaningless on their own; semantic tokens give them roles.

gray.$description: Neutral grey (hue stripped, C*≈0) — every surface, border, and ink tone. Held neutral (not warm) so no yellow film tints the editor, at lightnesses where all contrasts hold. base (50) is the single shared environment background for nvim, terminal and zellij; a soft off-white (not stark) so it reads calm, not glary.

red.$description: Errors, deletions, and the warm mode-accent. Hue locked to ~18° (clean crimson). A dark, low-chroma WARM colour reads as 'brick/brown' regardless of hue (brown is just dark desaturated orange), so 18° is chosen to move the mid-dark steps across a colour-NAMING boundary: the green and blue channels equalise (e.g. 600 #7A6060, G≈B), the orange cast drops out, and the dark steps read as 'wine/maroon' — still named red — not brick. 18° is deliberately the crossover point: far enough to kill the brown cast, not so far it tips into rose/pink (that starts ~15° and below). add-vs-delete holds ΔE≈5.5 under deuteranopia (carried by the preserved lightness offset, not hue). Light steps read as clean soft rose (git-standard deletion tint), dark steps as clean dark red.

amber.$description: Warm gold ramp — comment washes (light) and warnings (dark). Light steps are pinned to ~74-78° (warm wheat), NOT pure yellow ~90°: a desaturated 90° yellow greys toward dirty olive/khaki, so the light-end tints are rotated warmer to read as clean wheat/cream. The wash steps (100-300) share the other ramps' cool-monochrome tint budget (C≈0.011-0.045) so amber reads as barely-tinted warm paper on the highest-traffic surface (the comment band); the desaturation pulled it down to the same chroma as the neutrals, so amber now stays legibly warm by HUE (~78°) rather than by extra chroma — at this low chroma the 78° rotation is what keeps the band warm-stone rather than olive-grey. The whole ramp runs a single monotonic wheat->gold hue path (~78° light to ~72° gold dark, ~6° total spread); dark steps (400-900) carry the gold end for warning/terminal foregrounds.

blue.$description: Info, links, functions, and calm structural-content surfaces — doc backgrounds and diff.change ('modified'). Its light tiers carry doc.50 (doc/quote ground) and the diff-change pair change.100 (changed line) / changeText.200 (changed word); doc and diffs never co-occur in one buffer.

cyan.$description: Cyan ramp — terminal cyan channel (dark end, .600) and editor search highlights (light end, cyan.300 = all-matches band, cyan.400 = current match). Two non-overlapping regimes on one otherwise-unused hue.

violet.$description: Blue-violet — constants (dark end, .700) and interactive selection (light end, selection.match 100 / selection.primary 300). Two non-overlapping regimes on one hue: a different buffer and a different step, so they never collide.

alert.$description: OFF-RAMP alarm red — the ONE place the two-regime chroma model is broken on purpose. Every other ink step is pinned to the ~0.045 ceiling so 'every accent carries equal weight'; that uniformity is exactly what lets a single high-chroma element pop pre-attentively (a saturation feature-singleton). alert.fg sits at C≈0.14 — ~3x the ceiling — so an error MARK is the only saturated thing on screen and the eye finds it before it consciously looks. NOT on the eased L* ladder and NOT a ramp (a single named fg, not numeric steps) precisely so nobody mistakes it for a tunable accent: it is the reserved 'demands action' dimension, used by error diagnostics only. #B0454E (L≈0.54) sits on the red ramp's OWN 18° hue — deliberately NOT a foreign 'fire-engine' red — so it reads as the loud end of the theme's red, in-family, while still the most saturated thing present; AA on paper (4.97:1) so the sign glyph and undercurl read. The 3x chroma jump + the undercurl SHAPE make it CVD-robust (chroma magnitude and shape survive red-green deficiency where hue alone would not). Applied to the error MARKS — undercurl (sp), bold sign glyph, and the transient :messages/cmdline error line — foreground, no fill: the saturation IS the singleton, a background block would just read as a clunky box. The PERSISTENT in-buffer diagnostic message/virtual text stays on muted status.error (red.700), so a whole line of message isn't a slab of saturated red. Warnings stay on the muted amber ceiling, one tier down, so the alert axis is ordered: error shouts (at the mark), warning speaks, info/hint whisper.

semantic.$description: Layer 2 — roles in the Ergo Light language. Tool-agnostic: these describe meaning (a surface, an error, a string), never a tool. Every value aliases into a primitive ramp, so the whole system re-tunes from Layer 1. Two cross-cutting rules the roles below rely on rather than restate. HUE LANGUAGE: green=add/string, red=delete/error, blue=persistent content/structure (info, links, functions, doc & diff.change grounds), amber=annotation (comment band, TODO markers, warnings); the transient cursor-driven states get their own cool hues off the content hues so they never collide with persistent content — violet=live selection & matching-ref, cyan=search. CVD SEPARATION: where two roles would collapse on the red-green axis under deuteranopia/protanopia, they are offset by LIGHTNESS, not hue (the diff add>change>delete lightness ladder; constant/function/link on stepped violet/blue); where a non-colour cue is always present — the diff +/- gutter glyph, the error undercurl — that cue is the primary signal and the lightness offset is only the colour backstop.

base.$description: shared background for editor, terminal and zellij — soft neutral paper

cursorline.$description: current-line highlight — stepped to gray.200 so it is actually visible on paper

popup.$description: popup / telescope bg — one step off base so it reads as a layer, not just a border

key.$description: Selected block: active tab, current mode, cursor position. A grey keycap with ink text, calmer than a black fill.

primary.$description: body text / default fg — soft neutral dark (~8:1, softened from ~10:1 for the calmer cool-monochrome tuning), calm not harsh

muted.$description: hints, line numbers, muted UI (comments use comment.fg)

strong.$description: text on the strongest fills (current search match) — gray.900 keeps AA where text.primary drops to ~3.6:1

constant.$description: constants, numbers, booleans — violet.700, stepped darker than function (blue.600) for CVD lightness separation

link.$description: links / urls — blue.800, kept clear of constant (violet.700) under CVD; the two never share a buffer

error.$description: errors — darkest red, 2 steps below the warm mode-accent so the two never read alike

alert.$description: The 'demands action' tier — error only, kept separate from status.error so terminal/delta/zellij red stays muted (status.error = red.700) while the editor's error MARK shouts. One lever, error-scoped: the saturated undercurl + bold sign glyph only — foreground, no fill. The diagnostic message/virtual text rides muted status.error, not this, so only the small marks are loud. Warnings stay on amber one tier down. (Chroma-singleton physics: see primitive.alert.)

fg.$description: loud error MARK — undercurl + bold sign glyph only; message/virtual text uses status.error (muted)

mark.$description: Small armed-state mark (unsaved, recording) on surfaces; >=3:1. Never a fill.

primary.$description: active selection — violet.300, strong-tier (~1.5:1). Separates from cursorline (gray.200, ΔE≈6.9) and from diff.change (blue.100, ΔE≈10.5, ≈10.4 under deuteranopia/protanopia — carried by the L* offset, since the low chroma leaves little hue) so a selection inside a changed line reads clearly. Dark text ~5.2:1. Ink-tier chroma (the 0.045 ceiling), not wash chroma — a selection is meant to be seen.

match.$description: matched pair / reference — violet.100, paired with selection.primary; bracket-match and reference highlights track the cursor.

soft.$description: search match bg — cyan.300, strong/'pop' (~1.55:1). Clears the amber comment band (dE~7.8, deut ~6.5). ONE residual: overlaps selection (violet.300) at L~0.82 → dE~2.2 under deuteranopia — low severity (transient-vs-transient; the current match, cyan.400, stays clear of selection at dE~11.3 deut). Dark text ~5.3:1.

active.$description: current search / incsearch — one step above search.soft (cyan.400) so the match under the cursor out-reads the other matches (dE~11.2 from search.soft). Dark text ~3.6:1 — AA-large only; the softer cool-monochrome ink dropped this below AA-normal, acceptable because the current match is transient and cursor-driven.

fg.$description: comment foreground — aliased to text.secondary (same weight); comments are signal, meant to be read

bg.$description: normal comment band — amber.200 (standard-wash tier, ~1.30:1), a near-neutral warm-stone wash (C~0.017), not a gold block. A QUIET band by measurement. The prominence comments get in this theme comes almost entirely from the FOREGROUND weight (comment.fg = text.secondary, ~6:1 — comments read as strong as secondary UI text), not from the fill; the band's job is just to warm the region so the eye groups it, without shouting. Sole owner of amber.200 (diff.change lives on blue), so it never shares a step with another role.

high.$description: high-priority comment markers (TODO/FIXME/WARNING/NOTE) — amber.300, one step above the normal comment band (amber.200) so a marker out-reads surrounding comments.

add.$description: added lines — standard-tier tint (~1.29:1 on paper). Light wash step while diff.delete sits one tier darker; see diff.delete for why the pair is intentionally asymmetric (CVD).

addText.$description: word-level emphasis inside an added line (delta plus-emph / nvim DiffText) — one step above the line tint (strong tier) so the changed word out-reads the line, and lighter than diff.deleteText so add/delete word-patches separate by lightness under CVD.

change.$description: changed/modified lines (nvim DiffChange) — blue.100, whisper tier; top of the change>add>delete lightness ladder (add green.200 L≈0.87, delete red.300 L≈0.82; add/change ΔE≈4.8 deut, ≈4.9 normal). Deliberately faint (~1.13:1) for 'neutral modification'; the changed word (changeText, blue.200) carries the visible anchor. Matches VS Code's gutter (add=green / modified=blue / delete=red). Dark text ~7.2:1.

changeText.$description: word-level emphasis inside a changed line (nvim DiffText) — blue.200, one step ABOVE the change line (blue.100), mirroring add/addText (line at N, word at N+1). Gives the faint change band a visible anchor exactly on the changed span (~1.30:1 vs paper, dark text ~6.2:1) without making the whole line loud.

delete.$description: deleted lines — red.300, one tier ABOVE diff.add (L≈0.82 vs add's 0.87). Add is a light wash step, delete an ink step, so they separate in lightness and chroma both: the ΔL≈0.053 offset holds where an equal step (ΔL≈0.012) would collapse under CVD. Deletions read slightly stronger and warmer than additions.

deleteText.$description: word-level emphasis inside a deleted line (delta minus-emph) — red.400, one step below diff.addText (L≈0.71 vs 0.82, ΔL≈0.111) so a deleted word separates from an added word by lightness. Deeper than the delete line so the word still pops within its own line.

primary.$description: primary cursor block — kept near-black so the caret stays easy to spot

terminal.$description: The ANSI palette is a role a terminal plays, not a tool. Muted on purpose vs the editor accents. The 'white' channels are a hard light-theme constraint, not a loose choice: color 15 (bright white) must stay LIGHTER than color 7 (white) to preserve ANSI ordering, and on light paper 'lighter than the lightest AA-passing grey' is by definition sub-AA — so bright.white CANNOT reach AA as body text without breaking the ordering. gray.500 (3.4:1, AA-large) is therefore the provable optimum for bright.white, and white=gray.600 (4.9:1, AA) is as light as color 7 can go while passing AA. This only bites apps that explicitly paint body text in ANSI 7/15; the terminal's DEFAULT foreground is text.primary (gray.800, ~8.1:1), so ordinary uncoloured output is never affected.
